title: Backpressure wire protocol + telemetry sketch
content:
Context and intent:

This is a personal sketch for a compact wire protocol to carry backpressure signals between edge proxies, client SDKs, and Redwood ingress. The goal is pragmatic: an explicit minimal payload that is cheap to encode, easy to route through existing HTTP/2 and gRPC paths, and yields good telemetry without blowing up request volume.

Problem statement:
- Clients and edge proxies need a way to signal and observe resource pressure (queue lengths, token budgets, stall reasons) so that upstream callers can gracefully degrade or reroute.
- Current ad-hoc solutions (HTTP 429 with body, custom headers) are inconsistent and opaque to telemetry pipelines.
- We need a backwards-compatible, versioned, and human-decodable wire shape that fits both streaming RPCs and single-response flows.

Design goals (priority order):
1) Compact (small payloads, few fields)
2) Versioned and extensible without breaking older proxies
3) Easy to attach to HTTP/2 trailers, gRPC metadata, or a small JSON field for HTTP/1 flows
4) Telemetry-friendly: fields map directly to metrics and spans (reason codes, severity, latency delta)
5) Actionable: carries explicit suggested actions (throttle, reroute, degrade) not just descriptive state

Core concepts and types:
- signal_id: unique short id for correlating signals with request/session (base62, <=12 chars)
- severity: enum (ok, advisory, constrained, critical)
- token_budget_delta: integer (positive/negative) indicates how many tokens upstream can produce/should reduce
- queue_depth: small int (current length of local request queue)
- cpu_pressure_pct: integer 0-100 (optional)
- suggestion: enum (none, throttle, reroute, degrade_response, reject)
- hints: short bitmask for opt-in behaviors (e.g., allow_prefetch=1, allow_burst=2)

Wire encoding options considered:
- Tiny protobuf (binary, minimal blow-up) — good for gRPC paths and binary transports, requires proto rollout
- Compact JSON with fixed field keys (easier for HTTP/1 and debugging)
- Base64-URL single header value containing comma-separated kv pairs (most deployable today)

Proposal: dual-shape approach
- canonical binary proto definition for internal services and gRPC
- stable compact header encoding for proxies & external clients (text)

Header encoding specification (v1):
- Header name: x-rw-backpress (short, all lower-case)
- Value: version|signal_id|sev|budget|queue|cpu|suggest|hints
- Field separators: pipe (|) between fields; empty or missing fields omitted but order fixed
- Example: v1|s1Ab2C3|2|-40|12|72|2|5
  - v1: version 1
  - s1Ab2C3: signal id
  - 2: severity (0=ok,1=advisory,2=constrained,3=critical)
  - -40: token_budget_delta (upstream should reduce by 40 tokens)
  - 12: queue depth
  - 72: cpu pressure percent
  - 2: suggestion (1=throttle,2=reroute,3=degrade,4=reject)
  - 5: hints bitmask

Binary proto (v1) sketch (for internal gRPC):
- message BackpressureSignalV1 {
    string signal_id = 1; // base62 id
    enum Severity { OK = 0; ADVISORY = 1; CONSTRAINED = 2; CRITICAL = 3; }
    Severity severity = 2;
    int32 token_budget_delta = 3;
    uint32 queue_depth = 4;
    uint32 cpu_pressure_pct = 5;
    enum Suggestion { NONE = 0; THROTTLE = 1; REROUTE = 2; DEGRADE = 3; REJECT = 4; }
    Suggestion suggestion = 6;
    uint32 hints = 7;
  }

Attachment points:
- HTTP/2 + gRPC: attach proto on response trailers as binary metadata (x-rw-bp-bin) and include the header x-rw-backpress for easier logging.
- HTTP/1: include x-rw-backpress header. If request body contains a small JSON envelope (some integrations), include an embedded object under "redwood_backpressure": {..} (compatible shape).
- WebSockets/Edge proxies: same header on handshake response and periodically as ping messages with a small JSON snippet.

Telemetry mapping (one-to-one fields -> metrics/labels):
- severity -> counter per severity and histogram for downstream latency when severity >= constrained
- token_budget_delta -> gauge/timeline per tenant and per route
- queue_depth -> percentile histograms per POP/region
- suggestion -> event stream that triggers automated reroute decision engine logging
- signal_id -> traced across spans (attach as attribute) for debugging correlated incidents

Suggested metric names (initial):
- rw.bp.signals.count (tags: severity, suggestion, route, region)
- rw.bp.token_budget.delta (gauge)
- rw.bp.queue_depth (histogram)
- rw.bp.cpu_pressure.pct (gauge)

Span enrichment and sampling:
- If severity >= CONSTRAINED, force sampling of the trace for 1% additional retention for short incidents, 100% sampling if CRITICAL.
- Add attributes: backpressure.signal_id, backpressure.severity, backpressure.suggestion, backpressure.queue_depth.

Failure modes and compatibility:
- Unknown header or version: treat as no signal (ok) and record a telemetry counter for unknown-version to help migration.
- Malformed header: drop with a metric and do not apply action. Proxies should sanitize and never forward invalid encodings to clients.
- Race conditions: multiple signals can be issued along request path (edge, tenant-proxy, ingress). Use newest-by-timestamp semantics if present. Consider adding an optional epoch field in v2 for strong ordering.

Operational playbook (how to use at runtime):
1) Edge proxy emits advisory signals during high tail latency windows with suggestion=THROTTLE and budget=-20.
2) Client SDKs observe header and apply client-side token pacing for the next 5s window (configurable via hints bitmask for timeouts).
3) Ingest telemetry stream into a dedicated Backpressure topic; run correlator to detect cross-route pressure and automatically trigger reroute policies for suggestion=REROUTE with severity >= CONSTRAINED.

Quick example flows:
- Flow A (normal): backend returns no header -> client proceeds as usual.
- Flow B (short pressure): ingress returns x-rw-backpress: v1|xH3|1|-10|4||1|1 -> advisory, reduce tokens by 10, allow burst (hints=1).
- Flow C (critical): x-rw-backpress: v1|z9f|3|-100|40|95|2|0 -> critical, reroute suggested; client should fallback synchronously to alternate endpoint.

TODOs and open questions (prioritized):
- Decide canonical ordering for header fields and sign/verify for tenants that require authenticity.
- Add epoch/timestamp (int64) to avoid ordering races (v2).
- Define mapping from token_budget_delta to concrete client-side pacing algorithm (is -40 absolute tokens or tokens per second?). Need UX doc and client SDK shim.
- Prototype proto and header handling in node/py/go SDKs and the edge proxy; measure overhead on p99 request headers (size + parse cost).
- Define failure escalation thresholds and automated reroute thresholds (per-tenant).

Notes to self / implementation sketch:
- Keep header parsing cheap: split on '|' with a small inlined parser; avoid full JSON parsing on hot path.
- In Go: use strings.Index to find separators and strconv.Atoi for ints; cache parsed signal_id in small LRU for dedup suppression.
- Telemetry: emit an aggregated metric every 10s per POP to avoid high cardinality. Keep signal_id only for traces/logs, not as metric tag.

References and context links:
- Existing prefetch/backpressure experiments: notes in prefetched-backpressure-labbook (see linked artifacts)
- Related ticket: INF-912 (automated reroute rules)

End state (what success looks like):
- v1 header is implemented in edge proxy and ingress within 2 sprints, client SDKs receive and act on THROTTLE suggestions for known routes, and we have a telemetry pipeline that surfaces top-10 routes under pressure.

If this lands, next doc: compact proto registry, per-tenant authenticity, and a short SDK shim example (node/python) showing a 3-line client-side pacing implementation.

-- a.p.
